extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (computational number theorists, mathematicians, and developers using PARI/GP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions (quadratic fields, Dirichlet characters, integer arithmetic, and elliptic curve routines), describing required inputs, behavior, algorithms, and warnings. Intended to guide correct usage and interpretation of outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant D requirement (quadratic functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: D must be an integer congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4, which is not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is stated for quadgen, quadpoly, quadunit and related quadratic-field functions; when not satisfied the functions will error or behave as documented elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadgen semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: quadgen(GEN D) returns ω = (a + √D)/2 with a = 1 if D ≡ 1 mod 4, so that (1, ω) is an integral basis for the quadratic order of discriminant D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D must satisfy the discriminant requirement above; the returned value is a quadratic number suitable as basis element.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadhilbert behavior and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: quadhilbert(D) returns relative equations defining the Hilbert class field of the quadratic field of discriminant D. If D < 0 uses complex multiplication (Schertz’s variant). If D > 0 Stark units are used and in rare cases a vector of extensions may be returned whose compositum is the requested class field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When D>0 see bnrstark for details; function signature quadhilbert(GEN D, long prec) allows specifying precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadpoly canonical polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates the 'canonical' quadratic polynomial (in variable v) corresponding to the discriminant D, i.e. the minimal polynomial of quadgen(D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D must be integer congruent to 0 or 1 mod 4 and not a square. Library syntax GEN quadpoly0(GEN D, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadray ray class field equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation for the ray class field of conductor f for the quadratic field of discriminant D using analytic methods. A bnf for x^2 − D is also accepted in place of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For D<0 uses the σ function and Schertz’s method. For D>0 uses Stark’s conjecture and may return a vector of relative equations; see bnrstark. Syntax: GEN quadray(GEN D, GEN f, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadregulator input validation
rubrics_metrics.description: quadregulator(x) returns the regulator of the quadratic field of positive discriminant x; returns an error if x is not a discriminant (fundamental or not) or if x is a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is large, consider using quadclassunit instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadunit semantics and caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: quadunit(D) returns the fundamental unit of the real quadratic field Q(√D) where D is the positive discriminant of the field. If D is not a fundamental discriminant, this probably gives the fundamental unit of the corresponding order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D must be integer congruent 0 or 1 mod 4 and not a square; result is a quadratic number.

rubrics_metrics.name: ramanujantau assumptions and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: ramanujantau(n) computes Ramanujan’s tau function at n, assuming the truth of the GRH (used to compute class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields quickly using quadclassunit). Algorithm is in ~O(n^{1/2}) time using O(log n) space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all values up to N it is much faster to compute tauvec(N) = Vec(q*eta(q + O(q^N))^24) in ~O(N) time; repeated individual calls are ~O(N^{3/2}). Examples show major speedups: tauvec versus vector of ramanujantau calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomprime behavior and pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: randomprime({N=2^31}) returns a strong pseudoprime in [2, N−1]. A t_VEC N = [a,b] is allowed; a ≤ b and returns a pseudo prime a ≤ p ≤ b; if no prime exists in the interval the function will run into an infinite loop. If the upper bound is less than 2^64 the pseudo prime returned is a proven prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with intervals that contain no primes (infinite loop risk).

rubrics_metrics.name: removeprimes functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: removeprimes({x = []}) removes the primes listed in x from the prime number table. If x omitted lists current extra primes. x can be single integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: removeprimes(addprimes()) empties the extra prime table.

rubrics_metrics.name: sigma input types
rubrics_metrics.description: sigma(x,{k=1}) returns sum of the kth powers of the positive divisors of |x|. x and k must be of type integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN sumdivk(GEN x, long k). For k=1 GEN sumdiv(GEN n) is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtint definition
rubrics_metrics.description: sqrtint(x) returns the integer square root of x, i.e. the largest integer y such that y^2 ≤ x, where x is a non-negative integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example and comparison with floating sqrt illustrate exact integer return vs floating approximation. Syntax GEN sqrtint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtnint general n-th root
rubrics_metrics.description: sqrtnint(x,n) returns the integer n-th root of x, i.e. the largest integer y such that y^n ≤ x, where x is a non-negative integer. Special case n=2 is sqrtint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN sqrtnint(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: stirling numbers and performance guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: stirling(n,k,{flag=1}) returns Stirling numbers of the first kind s(n,k) (flag=1) or second kind S(n,k) (flag=2). n,k non-negative integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all s(n,k) are needed use the generating product x(x−1)...(x−n+1) and extract coefficients (divide-and-conquer product recommended). If many S(n,k) for same k use provided generating formula. Example helper functions vecstirling and vecstirling2 provided as variants; prefer these for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdedekind formula
rubrics_metrics.description: sumdedekind(h,k) returns the Dedekind sum attached to integers h and k, corresponding to fast implementation of s(h,k) = sum_{n=1}^{k-1} (n/k)*(frac(h*n/k) - 1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN sumdedekind(GEN h, GEN k).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdigits semantics and performance note
rubrics_metrics.description: sumdigits(n,{B=10}) returns the sum of digits of integer n when written in base B>1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sumdigits(123456789)=45. Note: sum of bits is returned by hammingweight; sumdigits is much faster than vecsum(digits(n,B)) when B=10 or a power of 2, and only slightly faster in other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: zncharinduce input and return
rubrics_metrics.description: zncharinduce(G, chi, N) with G attached to (Z/qZ)^* and chi a Dirichlet character (as t_VEC, t_INT, or t_COL) returns the character modulo N induced by chi, where N is a multiple of q. New modulus N may be given as t_INT, factorization matrix, or pair [N,factor(N)], or by idealstar(,N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show use with idealstar; accepts Conrey indices or vectors. See usage examples for convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: zncharisodd predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: zncharisodd(G, chi) returns 1 if and only if chi(−1) = −1 and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: chi may be given as t_VEC or Conrey index/log; example shown with idealstar(,8).

rubrics_metrics.name: znchartokronecker behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: znchartokronecker(G, chi, {flag=0}) if flag=0 returns the discriminant D if chi is real equal to the Kronecker symbol (D/·) and 0 otherwise. The discriminant D is fundamental iff chi is primitive. If flag=1 return fundamental discriminant attached to corresponding primitive character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for modulus 8 demonstrate both flag modes. Input chi may be t_VEC or Conrey index/log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conrey generator convention (znconreychar/log/exp)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conrey generators gp are defined for each prime divisor p of q (and possibly g4,g8 for p=2) with specific congruence conditions so that every m ∈ (Z/qZ)^* can be written uniquely as product of gp^{mp}. The Conrey logarithm of m is the vector (mp)_{p∈S_q} and Conrey character χ_q(m,·) maps each gp to e(mp/op).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions (znconreychar, znconreylog, znconreyexp) allow conversion between ordinary/Conrey logs and characters; note that including explicit generators in bid is unnecessary except for debugging. Examples illustrate round trips between representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreychar acceptance and output
rubrics_metrics.description: znconreychar(bid, m) returns the Dirichlet character attached to m∈(Z/qZ)^* via Conrey’s logarithm, expressed in standard PARI terms in terms of SNF generators bid.gen. m may be an integer or Conrey logarithm vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: passing non-coprime elements causes errors. Examples for modulus 8 and 55 given. Useless to include generators in bid except for debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreyconductor result format
rubrics_metrics.description: znconreyconductor(bid, chi, {&chi0}) returns the conductor of chi: if chi is primitive returns t_INT bid.mod, else returns pair [N, factor(N)]. If chi0 present set it to Conrey log of attached primitive character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The group G0 for the conductor is not computed as part of this function because it's only needed once per conductor; examples show format and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreyexp mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: znconreyexp(bid, chi) returns integer m∈(Z/qZ)^* such that znconreylog(bid, m) is chi. chi may be t_VEC on SNF generators or t_COL Conrey log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show consistency of znconreylog and znconreychar round-trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreylog computation and convenience inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: znconreylog(bid, m) returns the Conrey logarithm of m∈(Z/qZ)^*. It accepts m in several forms including integer m, ideallog result, ordinary discrete log on bid.gen, or a character t_VEC, converting to Conrey generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior for modulus with e2 cases is described; non-coprime inputs generate an error. Examples show conversions between representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: zncoppersmith parameter constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: zncoppersmith(P, N, X, {B=N}) finds integers x with |x| ≤ X such that gcd(N, P(x)) ≥ B using Coppersmith’s algorithm. X must be smaller than exp(log2 B/(deg(P) log N)). For B=N this means X < N^{1/deg(P)}. Some x larger than X may be returned if lucky. The smaller B (or larger X) the slower the routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coppersmith is strong for finding roots modulo general composite N. If N is prime or prime power, polrootsmod or polrootspadic will be much faster. Examples include factoring with known low-order digits and attacking low-exponent RSA with known padding; timings provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: znlog modes and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: znlog(x,g,{o}) computes discrete logarithms in two modes: if g is output of znstar (initialized) compute discrete log of x wrt generators; else g is explicit element in (Z/NZ)^* and compute discrete log of x in base g. Result is [] when x is not a power of g (but function may enter infinite loop in that case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter o can be provided as [ord, factor(ord)] to speed computations. The function uses Pohlig-Hellman, Shanks baby-step/giant-step (q < 2^32 small), and Pollard rho (q > 2^32). Shanks/Pollard require O(q^{1/2}) operations; Pollard rho cannot detect non-existence of solution (infinite loop risk). g may be p-adic number as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: znorder preconditions and output
rubrics_metrics.description: znorder(x,{o}) returns the order of x in multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^*. Returns an error if x is not invertible. The parameter o, if present, represents a non-zero multiple of the order of x; preferred format is [ord, factor(ord)] where ord = eulerphi(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN znorder(GEN x, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: znprimroot applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: znprimroot(n) returns a primitive root (generator) of (Z/nZ)^* whenever this group is cyclic, i.e. n = 4 or n = 2*p^k or n = p^k where p is an odd prime and k≥0. If group is not cyclic the result is undefined. If n is a prime power smallest positive primitive root is returned (may not hold for n=2*p^k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This function requires factoring p−1 for p above, which may be costly if p is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: znstar return formats and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: znstar(n,{flag=0}) gives the structure of the multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^*. For flag=0 returns abelian group [h,d,g] where h=φ(n) (G.no), d (G.cyc) is vector of di with di>1 and di|di−1, and g (G.gen) gives generators. flag=1 returns a bid structure without generators (saves time). flag=2 same as flag=1 with generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ZNstar(GEN N, long flag) with or-ed flags nf_GEN (include generators) and nf_INIT (return full bid) instead of numeric flags for better clarity. znstar(0) corresponds to Z^*.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellinit behavior and ell structure cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: ellinit([a1,a2,a3,a4,a6]) initializes and returns an ell structure for elliptic curve y^2 + a1xy + a3y = x^3 + a2x^2 + a4x + a6. Expensive data are skipped on initialization; they are computed dynamically when needed and cached. The precise layout of the ell structure is left undefined and should never be used directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An optional base field argument may be supplied if it cannot be inferred from coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: ell structure common members
rubrics_metrics.description: For all domains ell structure contains members: a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 (coefficients), b2,b4,b6,b8 (b-invariants), c4,c6 (c-invariants), disc (discriminant, required non-zero), j (j-invariant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members can be inspected (e.g. E.b4, E.disc) and are used by downstream functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: elliptic curves over R: periods and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: For curves over R (includes Q) ellperiods computes area, roots (complex roots of RHS g(x), ordered if real), and omega = [ω1, ω2] where ω1 is positive real period and ω2 is complex with τ = ω1/ω2 in Poincaré half-plane; normalized so that Im(ω2) < 0 and either Im(ω2)=0 when E.disc>0 or Im(ω2)=ω1/2. eta contains quasi-periods η1,η2 with Legendre relation η2 ω1 − η1 ω2 = 2πi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: many sources use inverse convention (ω2/ω1 has positive imaginary part); PARI uses τ = ω1/ω2 to make PSL2 action natural. Be aware of sign differences when comparing conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: curves over Qp input and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: For curves over Qp inputting a model defined over Q is advised. If an approximate model with t_PADIC coefficients is input it will be lifted to Q and computed from the lifted model. Currently only curves with multiplicative reduction (vp(j) < 0) are supported by non-trivial functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tate member returns [u2,u,q,[a,b],L,Ei] per Henniart-Mestre notation; L is Mazur-Tate-Teitelbaum L-invariant; technicalities on storage (quadratic t_POLMOD) if u not in Qp.

rubrics_metrics.name: curves over Fq members
rubrics_metrics.description: For curves over Fq members include p (characteristic), no = #E(Fq), cyc (cycle structure of E(Fq)), gen (generators), and group returns [no,cyc,gen] as abelian group structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These members allow direct inspection of group structure over finite fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: curves over Q: minimal model advice and elldata dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions should return correct results whether model is minimal or not, but minimal models are recommended (minor speed-up) especially when gcd(c4,c6) is easy to factor. ellminimalmodel replaces model by minimal one; ellchangepoint/ellchangepointinv convert points between models. Some routines (ellgenerators, ellidentify, ellsearch, forell) require optional package elldata (Cremona database) and need at least 2MB stack to avoid overflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When elldata is installed ellinit accepts alternative inputs like '11a1'; ellinit will load database chunks into memory for these functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: curves over number fields: nf and bnf members
rubrics_metrics.description: For curves over number fields ell structure includes nf (nf structure of number field) and bnf (bnf structure of number field) or raises an error if only nf is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some functions require bnf and will error if only nf present.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellL1 purpose and precision control
rubrics_metrics.description: ellL1(e,{r=0}) returns value at s=1 of derivative of order r of the L-function of elliptic curve e. Primary use: after using ellanalyticrank to determine order of vanishing, compute leading term at high accuracy to check or use Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify realprecision (or bitprec via ellL1_bitprec) for higher accuracy; examples show changing realprecision to 200 digits to compute ellL1(e,3).

rubrics_metrics.name: elladd: point addition
rubrics_metrics.description: elladd(E, z1, z2) returns sum of points z1 and z2 on elliptic curve E (ell structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple API wrapper; syntax GEN elladd(GEN E, GEN z1, GEN z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellak input/model requirements and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: ellak(E,n) computes coefficient a_n of L-function of elliptic curve E/Q (coefficients of newform of weight 2). E must be an ell structure over Q given by an integral model, not necessarily minimal though a minimal model will make function faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If model not minimal at bad primes function will be slower for n divisible by bad primes; examples show empirical timings comparing minimal vs non-minimal models.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellan requirements over number fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ellan(E,n) computes vector of first n Fourier coefficients a_k corresponding to elliptic curve E defined over a number field. If E defined over Q any model works (minimal recommended). Over general number fields model must be locally minimal at primes above 2 and 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate function ellanQ_zv returns t_VECSMALL to save memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellanalyticrank semantics and eps heuristic
rubrics_metrics.description: ellanalyticrank(e,{eps}) returns order of vanishing at s=1 of L-function and value of first non-zero derivative. To determine order, values less than eps are assumed zero; if eps omitted value half current precision is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate ranks 0..3 for known curves; use appropriate eps or increase precision if close-to-zero values occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellap trace of Frobenius usage and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: ellap(E,{p}) computes trace of Frobenius t for E, defined by #E(Fq) = q + 1 − t for primes of good reduction. If E over finite field omit p; if over Q p must be given (prime or maximal ideal). Equation must be integral at p but need not be minimal; minimal model is more efficient. Reduction may be singular — returns order of non-singular points in that case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithms used depend on situation: fast explicit formula for CM, Shanks-Mestre baby-step/giant-step for moderate q (~q^{1/4}), SEA for large primes (heuristic ~log(q)^4), and specialized methods in small characteristic (Mestre, Kohel, Satoh-Harley, Kedlaya). Availability of seadata package speeds computation for large characteristics. For number fields require idealprimedec format for p; if p above 2 or 3 assume input is locally minimal without checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellbil deprecation note
rubrics_metrics.description: ellbil(E, z1, z2) is a deprecated alias for ellheight(E,P,Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ellheight instead; syntax GEN bilhell(GEN E, GEN z1, GEN z2, long prec) exists for compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellcard functionality and parallels with ellap
rubrics_metrics.description: ellcard(E,{p}) computes order of group E(Fq) (as ellgroup would). If E over finite field omit p; if over Q p must be given. Equation need not be minimal; minimal model more efficient. Reduction allowed to be singular and returns order of non-singular points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar performance and algorithmic considerations as ellap; syntax GEN ellcard(GEN E, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellchangecurve coordinate changes
rubrics_metrics.description: ellchangecurve(E, v) changes curve coordinates using v = [u,r,s,t] mapping new coordinates x',y' to old coordinates by x = u^2 x' + r, y = u^3 y' + s u^2 x' + t. Special case v=1 denotes trivial coordinate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ellchangepoint and ellchangepointinv to map points along with curve change.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellchangepoint and inverse
rubrics_metrics.description: ellchangepoint(x, v) applies the coordinate change v = [u,r,s,t] to point(s) x; ellchangepointinv(x, v) applies inverse mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show mapping and inverse returning original points. Syntax GEN ellchangepoint(GEN x, GEN v) and GEN ellchangepointinv(GEN x, GEN ch).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellconvertname mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: ellconvertname(name) converts an elliptic curve name from elldata database string like '123b1' to triplet [conductor, isogeny class, index], and converts triplet back to curve name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for converting between human-readable names and numeric identifiers when elldata is installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: elldivpol division polynomial definition
rubrics_metrics.description: elldivpol(E,n,{v=x}) returns n-division polynomial f_n for curve E in variable v. For affine point P=(X,Y) we have [n]P = (φ_n(P) ψ_n(P) : ω_n(P) : ψ_n(P)^3) and f_n(X)=ψ_n(X) for n odd, f_n(X)=ψ_n(X,Y)(2Y + a1 X + a3) for n even. Examples and initial polynomials f1,f2,f4 given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for computations involving division points; polynomials are in Z[a1,a2,a3,a4,a6][X,Y].
